ex: The commandant of the base gave new orders.
The camp commandant was very strict with everyone.
Soldiers must report to the commandant every morning.
The new commandant visited the base last week.

SR.note: Here SR = Socialist Revolutionary (Russia, 1917). "Sr." after a name means "Senior".
ex: An SR was a member of the Socialist Revolutionary Party.
The SRs were a large party in Russia in 1917.
Many peasants voted for the SRs in the elections.
Our history book has a chapter about the SRs.

estimate.note: Often a verb: "Can you estimate the cost?" The noun ends like "-mit": an ES-ti-mit.

saloon.note: An Old West bar. In British English, also a car (US: "sedan").

rendezvous.note: Say "RON-day-voo". The plural is spelled the same: "rendezvous".

ex: This small battery gives one and a half volts.
Most wall outlets in Europe use 230 volts.
This phone charger works at five volts.
How many volts does this lamp need?

Chinatown.note: Always written with a capital C: "Chinatown".

Reich.note: Used mostly for Nazi Germany, as "the Third Reich."

puzzle.note: Often any game or problem to solve, like a crossword puzzle. A picture one is a "jigsaw puzzle".

patriotism.note: Uncountable: a lot of patriotism (not "a patriotism").

romantic.note: Most often an adjective: "a romantic dinner", "a romantic movie".

textile.note: Usually plural: "textiles". One kind of cloth is "a fabric".

ex: The remake is better than the original movie.
They announced a remake of the old video game.
I didn't like the remake at all.
Studios make too many remakes of old films these days.
"Cool" is common slang for "good".
Teenagers use a lot of slang when they text.
This word is old slang from the 1990s.
I don't understand all the new slang my kids use.
Talking about money is a taboo in some families.
There is a strong taboo against eating pork there.
Death is still a taboo for many people.
She broke a social taboo by speaking out.
The paladin rode out to defend the king.
The twelve paladins appear in many old French legends.
In this game, I usually play as a paladin.
The paladin raised his shield and charged.

retard.note: Highly offensive slur; do not use it.

Tao.note: Usually "the Tao": in Chinese thought, the natural way of the world.

reboot.note: Also a computer restart: "The computer needs a reboot." Often a verb too.
ex: The studio is making a reboot of the old series.
Fans did not like the reboot of their favorite show.
Is this movie a reboot or a sequel?
The reboot has new actors and a darker story.
A strong cyclone hit the island last night.
The cyclone destroyed hundreds of homes near the coast.
Many people left their homes before the cyclone arrived.
Cyclones bring strong winds and heavy rain.

march.note: Most often "March" is the month: "My birthday is in March." Also a verb: "to march".
ex: The soldiers went on a long march through the hills.
Thousands of people joined the peace march downtown.
The army band played a march at the parade.
The march lasted three days without a break.

vending.note: Usually in "vending machine": a machine that sells snacks or drinks.

raft.note: Often a flat boat made of logs: "They built a raft." Also "a raft of" = a lot of.
ex: We went down the river in a rubber raft.
Everyone in the raft must wear a helmet.
The raft hit a rock in the fast water.
Ten people can fit in this big raft.
He is a rich capitalist who owns three factories.
Capitalists invest money to make a profit.
The workers protested against the capitalists.
She calls herself a proud capitalist.

bong.note: A water pipe for smoking drugs. Also the deep sound of a big bell.
ex: Police found a bong in his room.
This shop sells glass bongs and pipes.
He hid the bong before his parents came home.
A bong is a pipe that uses water.

hybrid.note: Also an adjective: "a hybrid car", "hybrid work".

veto.note: Plural: "vetoes". Also a verb: "to veto a law".
ex: The president used his veto to stop the new law.
Each member country has a veto on this decision.
My mom has a veto over where we go on vacation.
The governor's veto stopped the tax plan.

zodiac.note: Usually "the zodiac". Your sign is your "zodiac sign" or "star sign".
ex: There are twelve signs in the zodiac.
Which sign of the zodiac were you born under?
She checks her zodiac sign in a magazine every week.
The zodiac is based on groups of stars.

canon.note: Do not mix it up with "cannon", a big gun. In fan talk, "canon" is the official story.
ex: This novel is now part of the literary canon.
The church still follows canon law on marriage.
The choir sang a canon, with voices starting one by one.
These old texts are not part of the official canon.

decor.note: Uncountable: the decor, some decor (not "a decor"). Also spelled "décor".
ex: I love the decor in this restaurant.
The decor is simple and modern.
She changed the decor of her living room.
The decor in our hotel room looks very old.
Please send me the invoice by Friday.
The invoice is due in thirty days.
I paid the last invoice online this morning.
The invoice shows all the costs for the repair.

handmade.note: An adjective in English: "handmade soap". It is not used alone as a noun.
ex: She sells handmade jewelry on her website.
This handmade sweater was a gift from my grandma.
I always buy handmade soap at the market.
The small shop near our school sells handmade toys.

Buddhism.note: Always written with a capital B: "Buddhism".
ex: Buddhism started in India about 2,500 years ago.
She became interested in Buddhism after a trip to Asia.
Buddhism teaches peace and kindness to all living things.
Many people in Thailand practice Buddhism.

joker.note: Also a person who likes to joke or play tricks: "He's a real joker."
ex: In this game, the joker can replace any card.
He played his joker at the last moment.
A normal deck of cards has two jokers.
I got the joker and won the game.
The movie is about a tribe of cannibals.
The cannibal was caught by police.
Some spiders are cannibals and eat other spiders.
The story about cannibals scared the kids.

easy.note: Also in "Take it easy" = relax, don't worry.
ex: This test was easy, so I finished early.
Is it easy to get to the station from here?
The recipe is quick and easy to make.
This game is too easy for me now.

superman.note: Most often "Superman" is the comic book hero. As a common noun: a very strong, able man.

caviar.note: Uncountable: some caviar, a lot of caviar (not "a caviar").
ex: We tried black caviar at the party.
Real caviar is very expensive in most stores.
She served caviar on small crackers.
The restaurant is famous for its caviar.
